This notebook goes through one decision: see what you may trade, download prices, build a portfolio, check it and submit it. Run it chunk by chunk; nothing is sent until the `submit()` chunk.

## Setup

Install once, in a terminal in your project folder, with [uvr](https://github.com/nbafrank/uvr) (0.4.8 or later):

```sh
uvr add advanced-empirical-finance/aefsim/r tidyfinance dplyr tidyr
```

```{r}
library(aefsim)
library(tidyfinance)
library(dplyr)
```

Save your team's token once: `set_token()` asks for it, asks where to save it and offers to add the file to `.gitignore`. Never paste the token into a script or notebook you share.

```{r}
set_token()   # once per project
```

## What can we trade, and under which rules?

```{r}
universe <- get_universe()
close_date <- max(universe$close_date)   # the latest close
close_date
count(universe, sp500)
```

`get_universe()` lists the stocks you can buy: common stocks on NYSE, NYSE American and Nasdaq that closed at $5 or more. A stock you hold that drops below $5 stays in your portfolio; you may keep or reduce it, but not buy more.

```{r}
get_parameters()                            # costs, shorting, leverage, position cap; applies_next marks the current rules
get_calendar() |> filter(is_next)           # the next trading day and its deadline, 09:00 New York time
```

## Prices

The simulation does not serve prices. tidyfinance downloads them from Yahoo Finance, the same source the simulation trades at.

```{r}
candidates <- universe |> filter(sp500) |> pull(ticker)
prices <- download_data("Stock Prices", symbols = candidates, start_date = close_date - 365, end_date = close_date)
```

## A simple rule

As an example (not a recommendation): the 20 S&P 500 stocks with the lowest volatility over the past year, equal weight.

```{r}
volatility <- prices |>
  arrange(symbol, date) |>
  group_by(symbol) |>
  mutate(ret = adjusted_close / lag(adjusted_close) - 1) |>
  summarise(vol = sd(ret, na.rm = TRUE) * sqrt(252), days = n()) |>
  filter(days >= 200)

weights <- volatility |>
  slice_min(vol, n = 20) |>
  transmute(ticker = symbol, weight = 1 / n())
weights
```

Weights are fractions of your portfolio's value, in a tibble with the columns `ticker` and `weight`. Tickers you leave out get zero, so this replaces your whole portfolio; whatever does not add up to one stays in cash.

## Check, then submit

```{r}
check <- validate(weights, close_date = close_date)
check
```

`validate()` runs every check the simulation runs and stores nothing. When it says OK, submit. The weights trade at the next market open whose deadline (09:00 New York time, usually 15:00 in Copenhagen) has not passed; the check shows that date. The rationale is your decision log: write down what you expect and why.

```{r}
result <- submit(
  weights, close_date = close_date,
  rationale = "Low-volatility tilt: equal weight in the 20 least volatile S&P 500 stocks over the past year."
)
result
```

Changed your mind? Submit again (the last accepted submission before the deadline is the one that trades), or `cancel(result$submission_id)`.

## The next morning

Trades happen at the US open; results appear after the nightly update.

```{r}
get_submissions()
get_portfolio() |> tidyr::unnest(positions)   # one row per position
get_performance()$summary
get_leaderboard()
```
